'''David A. Cardwell''' is a [[British people|British]] [[Superconductivity|superconducting]] engineer.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/today/hi/today/newsid_8803000/8803020.stm|author=BBC|date=2010|access-date=12 December 2014|title=Today: Friday 9th July}}</ref> He is a [[Academic ranks in the United Kingdom|Professor]] of [[superconducting engineering|Superconducting Engineering]], former Pro-Vice-Chancellor for Strategy and Planning at the [[University of Cambridge]] (2018-2024), former head of the [[University of Cambridge]] [[Department of Engineering, University of Cambridge|Department of Engineering]] (2014-2018), former co-director of the KACST-Cambridge Research Centre and a fellow of [[Fitzwilliam College]].<ref name="officialbio">{{cite web|url=http://www-g.eng.cam.ac.uk/bulk_sucon/dc135/|author=University of Cambridge|date=2014|accessdate=12 December 2014|title=Prof. David Cardwell FREng}}</ref>  In 2012, Cardwell was elected as a fellow of the [[Royal Academy of Engineering]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.raeng.org.uk/about-us/people-council-committees/the-fellowship/list-of-fellows?q=cardwell|accessdate=12 December 2014|author=Royal Academy of Engineering|date=2012|title=List of Fellows - Cardwell, Professor David FREng|archive-date=13 December 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141213023536/http://www.raeng.org.uk/about-us/people-council-committees/the-fellowship/list-of-fellows?q=cardwell|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Education==

Cardwell studied at the [[University of Warwick]] ([[BSc]] 1983, [[PhD]] 1987).<ref name="officialbio"/>  He is a fellow of the [[Institute of Physics]] and the [[Institution of Engineering and Technology]].<ref name="officialbio"/>

==Degrees==
*DSc, Warwick University, 2015
*ScD, University of Cambridge, 2014 
*MA, University of Cambridge, 1995 
*PhD, Warwick University, 1987 
*BSc, Warwick University, 1983<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://bulk-sucon.eng.cam.ac.uk/dc135/|title = Bulk Superconductivity Group - Prof. David Cardwell FREng}}</ref>

==Research interests==
Professor Cardwell's research interests include the processing, modelling and characterisation of bulk superconductors for high-field engineering applications. Materials of particular interest include high-temperature superconductors within the (RE)BCO family and MgB2.{{clarify|What are these jargon terms?|date=February 2020}}<ref name="officialbio2">{{cite web|url=http://www.eng.cam.ac.uk/profiles/dc135|author=University of Cambridge|date=2015|accessdate=19 March 2015 | title=David Cardwell Department of Engineering}}</ref> He has authored or co-authored more than 370 published papers.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www3.eng.cam.ac.uk/research_db/publications/dc135|title=Publications by Prof. David Cardwell &#124; Department of Engineering}}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

==Current position==

*Visiting Professor at the University of Hong Kong
*Adjunct Professor at the Shanghai University of Science and Technology
*Member of the Hong Kong Government University Grants Committee
*Treasurer of the European Society for Applied Superconductivity
*Member of the Advisory Board of Superconductor Science and Technology
*Chairman of the Thomas School Development Steering Committee (Ambright Education Group)<ref>{{cite web |title=剑桥副校长亲临，世界名校中国英才遴选中心上海基地落户上海安生学校 |url=https://zhuanlan.zhihu.com/p/610351501 |website=zhihu |access-date=6 June 2025}}</ref>

==Distinctions==

*Fellow of the Royal Academy of Engineering
*Fellow of the [[Institute of Physics]]
*Fellow of the IET<ref name="officialbio"/>

==Prizes==

*The Society of Automotive Engineering (SAE) Arch T. Colwell Merit Award, 2008<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.engii.org/scet2013/ShowOrganizerDetails.aspx?personID=2152|title=SCET2013_Show Organizer Details}}</ref>
*PASREG prize for excellence in the processing of bulk superconductors, 2001<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www2.warwick.ac.uk/newsandevents/pressreleases/ballet_opera_tv/|title = Ballet, opera, TV, WMD and tropical medicine all feature in latest honorary degrees announced by University of Warwick}}</ref>
